topic: Iron went up, free T3 went down: a retest that pointed back to Hashimoto's
angle: STAR client story (C09): Hashimoto's with critically low iron and B12; iron doubled; ferritin rose but free T3 kept falling, pointing to autoimmunity; advised to involve her prescribing doctor. Lesson: a number moving the wrong way is information; retest thyroid while fixing iron/B12 and share every result with your doctor.

hook: Her iron finally started going up. The thyroid number I was watching went the other way.
draft:
Her iron finally started going up. The thyroid number I was watching went the other way.

She's in her 40s and has Hashimoto's, where the immune system attacks the thyroid. When she came to me, her iron stores and her B12 were both critically low.

The plan looked simple. Rebuild iron and B12 first, because in my practice low iron is one of the first things I fix in women with thyroid problems. Then retest and watch the thyroid.

So we doubled her iron and retested.

Her iron stores rose from 25 to 36. That part worked.

Her free T3 didn't. Free T3 is the active thyroid hormone, the form your cells actually use. It kept falling from one test to the next.

Iron was going up and free T3 was going down. To me, that pointed back to the autoimmune side of her Hashimoto's. I advised her to take these results to the doctor who prescribes her thyroid medicine.

A number moving the wrong way feels like failure. It's information. It told us iron alone wasn't the answer for her, and that her doctor needed to see it.

If you're working on iron or B12 with Hashimoto's, retest your thyroid too. And share every result with your doctor, including the ones that went the wrong way.

#Hashimotos #ThyroidHealth

With iron rising and free T3 dropping, I read it as the autoimmune side of her Hashimoto's showing up, and I advised her to take the results to the doctor who prescribes her thyroid medicine.
